title: The Board's side is a constant; its 764-line fixture is unreachable
body:
## Summary
app/(studio)/board/_port/port.ts:35 hard-codes `SIDE = "real"`, while every other studio port reads GRAVITONE_PRODUCE_SIDE, so ./fixture.ts and ./fixtureData.ts (764 lines) run nowhere.

## Description
CLAUDE.md ("each reading through a `_port` whose side is `GRAVITONE_PRODUCE_SIDE`") and the context map's description both say the Board switches on that variable. The code does not: port.ts:35 is `export const SIDE: "fixture" | "real" = "real"` (wave C flipped it, 26820a6d), and the five other ports (projects, part, library, style, scout) read the env. pipeline/cx-screens.mjs:90 depends on this (it follows the Floor's first pile because the Board answers from the real side even on the fixture lane). Consequences: (1) fixture.ts enforces six kernel rules that no test exercises and no runtime reaches (`git grep fixtureBoard|resetFixture` outside _port = 0); (2) it has already drifted from the kernel - its commit and return do not advance `rev`, the kernel's do (real.ts commit returns r.value.rev from the committed act); (3) a fixture-lane dev server opens the kernel through GRAVITONE_STORE_PATH for the Board alone. Two coherent fixes: wire SIDE to GRAVITONE_PRODUCE_SIDE (and re-point cx-screens' board ids and tests/live board specs at the fixture seeds), or delete fixture.ts + fixtureData.ts (keeping `toneWav`, which library/fixture-tone cites) and correct CLAUDE.md. Which one is the operator's call: it decides what the fixture lane photographs.

## Flow
- read app/(studio)/board/_port/port.ts:35 against app/(studio)/projects/_port/port.ts:50
- `git grep -n "fixtureBoard\|resetFixture"` -> only port.ts and fixture.ts
- option A: SIDE from env; run tests/live board-exit + cx-capture board on the fixture lane
- option B: delete the two files, move toneWav, edit CLAUDE.md's Where-things-live line

## Expected impact
The operator and every agent reading CLAUDE.md stop being told the Board has a fixture side it does not use; either 764 lines leave or they start earning their keep. Could break: option A changes what the live lane's board screens draw.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one side switch, as the other ports have, or no dead side
Before: 5 of 6 studio ports read GRAVITONE_PRODUCE_SIDE; Board 0; fixture reached by 0 consumers
After: 6 of 6, or the fixture deleted (0 dead lines)
Method: probe - grep of the six ports and the fixture's importers; the choice between the arms is not measurable
Result: better
Gate: direction

title: A decided desk says 'weir clear' when the rail failed to load
body:
## Summary
When listPackets fails, loadBoard hands the Board an empty rail (now logged, 72b49e5d), and DecidedDesk draws the `weir clear` chip because `next` is undefined - a claim about the work that is false.

## Description
app/(studio)/board/_board/load.ts returns `rail: []` on a list failure; Board.tsx computes `nextOpen` from that rail; app/(studio)/board/_board/DecidedDesk.tsx:38 renders `<Chip label="weir clear" tone="emerald" />` whenever `next === undefined`. A locked store or a failed Weir read therefore tells the operator there is nothing left to decide. Fixed looks like: BoardLoad carries `railError`, the Board passes it down, and the decided desk's foot shows the store's sentence (ErrorLine) instead of the chip. The sheet entry app/(studio)/@sheet/(.)board/[packet]/page.tsx (outside this context's paths) must pass it too, which is why this is not Lane A.

## Flow
- the store refuses listPackets -> loadBoard rail [] -> Board nextOpen undefined -> DecidedDesk foot = weir clear
- build: BoardLoad.railError; both pages pass it; DecidedDesk foot shows ErrorLine when set

## Expected impact
The operator is never told the Weir is clear when the Board could not read it. Could break: the decided desk's foot layout on the sheet.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no false 'weir clear' on a failed rail
Before: 1 of 1 rail failures drawn as 'weir clear' (walked: load.ts -> Board.tsx nextOpen -> DecidedDesk.tsx:38)
After: 0 of 1, by a render test of DecidedDesk with railError set
Method: simulation - the sheet page is outside this round's paths and no DecidedDesk render test exists in this context
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/board/_board/DecidedDesk.tsx:38  foot={next === undefined ? <Chip label="weir clear" ... /> : ...}
app/(studio)/board/_board/load.ts  rail: list.ok ? list.value.packets : []
instrument: a react-dom/server render of DecidedDesk with next undefined and railError set (packages/ui/test/board-render.test.ts idiom): asserts the store's sentence and no 'weir clear' (0/1 today)

title: A pagehide beacon over 64 KB is dropped and nobody knows
body:
## Summary
Board.tsx `beacon` ignores navigator.sendBeacon's boolean; browsers refuse payloads over ~64 KB, so a large queued flush is lost silently.

## Description
app/(studio)/board/_board/Board.tsx:39 calls `navigator.sendBeacon(...)` and discards its return; packages/ui/src/board/boardGate.ts:91 hands it every queued change in one body. The keepalive door accepts up to 500 changes and a 256 KB body (keepalive/route.ts), but the user agent caps a beacon's queued data at 64 KiB and returns false past it. A cull flush with notes (note up to 2000 chars) crosses that at ~30 noted changes. Fixed looks like: chunk the changes under ~60 KB per beacon, and fall back to `fetch(..., { keepalive: true })` when sendBeacon returns false. review-queues (hitl-approval) names write-back reliability as a gate's duty.

## Flow
- operator notes 40 rejects quickly and closes the tab inside the write window
- flushOnHide -> beacon(id, rev, 40 changes ~ 85 KB) -> sendBeacon returns false -> verdicts lost
- build: chunk in Board.tsx beacon (or boardGate), each chunk its own sendBeacon

## Expected impact
Verdicts typed just before a tab closes survive regardless of note length. Could break: chunked flushes apply as several kernel acts (one undo step each).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no verdict lost to the beacon size cap
Before: changes delivered when the queued body > 64 KB: 0 (walked; sendBeacon spec)
After: all, chunked
Method: simulation - no DOM in the vitest lane; a fake sendBeacon that refuses > 64 KB in a boardGate test would take the figure
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/board/_board/Board.tsx:39  navigator.sendBeacon(`${boardFor(id)}/keepalive`, new Blob([JSON.stringify({ rev, changes })]))  // return ignored
packages/ui/src/board/boardGate.ts:91  beacon(id, revs.get(id) ?? 0, [...changes].map(...))
instrument: packages/ui/test/board-gate.test.ts case with a beacon stub that returns false over 64 KiB: count changes delivered for a 40-change noted flush (0 today)

title: Every load of a decided packet re-reads its v1 record to be refused
body:
## Summary
real.ts loadPacket calls `plan(id)` - the adapter's full v1 read - before checking the stored packet's state, so each render of a committed dojo/strips packet re-reads (and hashes) its media only to fall back to the bare view.

## Description
app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:138 `const planned = await plan(id)` runs for every held packet; for a committed run the adapter's `packet()` refuses and the view falls back (real.ts header: 'when v1 no longer plans the packet (a committed run refuses)'). board-decision-adapters (wave 2, open B card) measured dojo and strips hashing media serially, two stats per file, inside `read`. Fixed looks like: read head state first; for a non-open packet, skip the plan unless the adapter declares it can still present a decided run (a capability flag), keeping words where v1 still plans. Risk is the labels a decided desk shows today for sources whose adapter still plans after commit.

## Flow
- open a committed dojo packet's page -> loadBoard -> loadPacket -> plan -> adapter.read hashes N arms -> packet() refuses -> bare view
- build: head(r,id).state check before plan; adapter capability for decided presentation

## Expected impact
Decided desks open without a media re-hash; the rail and the Ledger link render sooner. Could break: a decided desk that today shows labels from a still-planning adapter.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - no v1 read for a packet that cannot be planned
Before: 1 adapter.read per decided-packet load (walked through real.ts:134-145)
After: 0 for sources whose adapter refuses decided runs
Method: simulation - needs a counting adapter in board-real.test.ts over a committed packet
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:136-140  const held = exists(store, id); ... const planned = await plan(id); if (held.value) { if (planned.ok) ...; const v = view(store, id, undefined, ...)
instrument: a counting adapter in tests/next-server/board-real.test.ts: adapter.read calls per loadPacket of a committed packet (1 today), with present.items unchanged for the sources that still plan
drain_note: needs a DecisionAdapter capability flag across adapters

title: A Weir pile past the rail's 100 rows is listed again as unopened
body:
## Summary
real.ts listPackets builds its `held` set from a 100-row page; a kernel packet beyond it whose v1 pile is still in the Weir is re-listed as an unopened open pile with rev 0.

## Description
app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:164-166 reads `listPacketSummaries(r, { limit: 100 })` (ordered open first, then newest) and `held = new Set(listed.packets.map(id))`; each Weir item is skipped only if `held.has(w.packetId)`. A decided packet older than the 100th row whose v1 pile is still pending (a stuck apply, so v1 never moved) therefore appears on the rail a second time, as `state: "open", rev: 0`, and opening it shows the decided desk. Fixed looks like: ask the kernel for the Weir items' ids directly (`SELECT id FROM packets WHERE id IN (...)`), not the page.

## Flow
- 100+ packets decided; packet P (older) committed with a stuck apply; v1 still lists P's pile
- listPackets -> held lacks P -> unopened summary for P (open, rev 0) on the rail
- build: an exists-batch read for the Weir ids

## Expected impact
The rail never shows a decided packet as open. Could break: nothing visible; one extra indexed read per rail.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the rail's open set agrees with the kernel
Before: walked: a decided packet past row 100 with a pending v1 pile is listed open (1 of 1)
After: 0 of 1
Method: simulation - reproducing needs 101 packets and a stuck apply in board-real.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:164  const listed = k.value.read((r) => listPacketSummaries(r, { limit: 100 }));
app/(studio)/board/_port/real.ts:166  const held = new Set<string>(listed.value.packets.map((p) => p.id));
instrument: board-real.test.ts case: open+commit 101 packets via a stub adapter, keep one's apply stuck with its pile in the stub Weir; count rail rows naming it (2 today, 1 after)
